A0253.title: Order Book Anomaly Monitoring
A0253.definition: Collect order-book placements, cancellations, executions, queue changes, and spread movement to identify spoofing, layering, and abnormal order-book pressure.
A0253.description:
Order book anomaly monitoring collects order-by-order submissions, executions, cancellations, order lifecycles, queue positions, bid/ask depth, spreads, and cross-account linkage features to build a normal order-book baseline. Thresholds, rules, sequence models, and anomaly detection can identify rapid cancellation after large orders, layering, sudden disappearance of order-book pressure, and prices following false depth.

This control detects market microstructure manipulation, order-book spoofing, and liquidity illusion. It should be combined with account linkage, venue rules, market-maker exemptions, and manual review to avoid misclassifying legitimate market making, rebalancing, or liquidity management.
A0253.limitation: Order-book behavior varies by instrument liquidity, session, market-making strategy, and volatility, so simple cancellation-rate or order-size thresholds can misfire. Attackers can reduce order size, split across accounts and venues, or mimic market-making rhythm, requiring graph linkage and cross-market review.
